title: Inbox by Gmail
lede: Google’s experimental email client, launched in 2014 as one of the first full Material Design apps: a blue app bar, white cards, and a red action button.
summary: Blue app bar, bundled mail on white cards over pale gray, and a round red plus button. Google, 2014.

source.label: Official Gmail Blog: “An inbox that works for you” (22 October 2014)

evidence.note: Opened the two images in Google’s announcement post on 28 September 2026: *inbox-nexus6-500.png* (500 × 884, the app on a Nexus 6) and *bigtopblog_fullres.gif* (1000 × 592, a close-up of a Purchases bundle). Not stored.

styles.note: A clear example: blue primary app bar, white cards and list rows on pale gray, and a red floating action button in the lower right.

context: Sundar Pichai announced Inbox on the Official Gmail Blog on 22 October 2014 as “a completely different type of inbox”. [Gmail Blog](https://gmail.googleblog.com/2014/10/an-inbox-that-works-for-you.html).

Wikipedia: Inbox was announced on an invitation-only basis on 22 October 2014, released to the public on 28 May 2015, and shut down on 2 April 2019. [Wikipedia: Inbox by Gmail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inbox_by_Gmail).
observed: A bright blue app bar holds a hamburger menu, the white title “Inbox”, a pin toggle, and a search glyph. The status bar above it is a darker blue.

Messages sit in white rows on a pale gray ground, with gray section labels “Today” and “Yesterday”. A Purchases bundle is a white card with a soft shadow and square corners, holding flat gray inner tiles with product photos.
Bundle labels are colored words: brown “Purchases”, cyan “Promos”, each with a count on a light tint of the same color.
A round red action button with a white plus floats over the lower right corner of the list with a soft shadow.
interpretation: Inbox uses the accent rule in its textbook form: a blue primary and a red action button, with category colors used only for small labels.
borrow: Give each content category one hue and use it only for its label and a light tint behind the count.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The product and images belong to Google.
